name: The Vanguard
body:
Entropy is one of the least understood forces in the Multiverse. Usually associated with scientific fields such as thermodynamics, it also influences magic and metaphysics. It is a force associated with change, randomness, disorder, and uncertainty—guaranteeing that nothing stays the same forever. As the saying goes: “The only constant is change.” (Or, in the slightly more cynical version: “Things fall apart.”)

As a vanguard, you are a master of entropy—understanding this force in a way that no one else does, and tapping into it in a way that no one else can. Even your own injuries become potential sources of primal, destructive energy that you can turn against your enemies.

Role: You are a front-line warrior who excels at creating havoc and using the chaos of the battlefield to fuel your combat abilities.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: 1d10.

Starting Age Self-Taught.

Starting Wealth: 4d6 × 10 (average 140 gp).

Class Skills

Your class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are Acrobatics (Dex). Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the vanguard class.

Table 1: The Vanguard

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

You are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields).

Entropic Pool (Su)

You can harness the energy of entropy released around you, allowing you to arrest, accelerate, or even reverse the typical course of events. This energy takes the form of a pool of Entropy Points (EP). You can have a maximum number of EP in your entropic pool equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1); certain feats and abilities (such as the Extra Entropy feat) can increase this maximum.

You can gain EP only when involved in a combat encounter that includes a significant enemy (usually a foe with at least half as many Hit Dice as you, subject to your GM’s discretion). At the end of combat, you lose any Entropy Points you have remaining. In addition to methods granted by vanguard aspects, you can gain Entropy Points in the followings ways:

Roll Initiative: You gain 1 EP when you roll initiative in combat with a significant enemy. If you are at least 10th level, you instead gain 2 EP. If you are at least 19th level, you instead gain 3 EP.
Charge: If you charge a significant enemy, you gain 1 EP.
Move: Each time you move at least your base movement speed during your turn, you gain 1 EP.
Score a Critical Hit: If you confirm a critical hit against a significant enemy with an entropic strike or entropic weapon, you gain 1 EP.
Take Damage: Each time you sustain hit point damage equal to or greater than twice your character level from a single attack or effect (after applying any ability to reduce that damage, such as 3 DR, energy resistance, or the mitigate class feature), you gain 1 EP.
Take Damage from a Critical Hit: If you take hit point damage from a critical hit, you gain 1 EP, in addition to any you gain from the attack’s normal damage.

Entropy Points can be expended in various ways, some of which you gain through vanguard aspects and disciplines.

Entropic Defense: As long as you have at least 1 EP in your entropic pool, you gain a +1 dodge bonus to your Armor Class.
Entropic Enhancement: By spending 1 EP as a swift action, you can enhance your entropic strikes or one of your entropic weapons with the power of pure, unbridled entropy. The chosen attack gains a +1 enhancement bonus for 1 round. For every 5 vanguard levels you possess, this bonus increases by 1, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. This bonus stacks with any existing enhancement bonuses the weapon might have, to a maximum of +5. For every additional EP you spend, the duration of this effect is extended by 1 additional round.
Entropic Movement: Whenever you move or charge, you can expend 1 or more EP as a swift action to gain an enhancement bonus to any one movement type that you have. For every EP that you spend, your speed increases by 10 feet for that movement type for 1 round.
Entropic Strike (Su)

At 1st level, you gain Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat.

Your unarmed strikes are always charged with the power of entropy, making them more devastating. Your entropic strikes are usually lethal, but you can make them deal nonlethal damage if you wish. Entropic strike damage for Medium vanguards is given on Table 1 (see page 2); see Table 2, below, for vanguards of other sizes.

Table 2: Entropic Strike Damage By Size
Level	Tiny	Small	Large	Huge
1–3	1d3	1d4	1d8	2d6
4–7	1d4	1d6	2d6	3d6
8–11	1d6	1d8	2d8	3d8
12–15	1d8	1d10	3d6	4d6
16–19	1d10	2d6	3d8	4d8
20	2d6	2d8	4d8	6d8
Entropic Weapon (Su)

In addition to your unarmed strikes, you can charge weapons you wield with the power of entropy. Any weapon you select with the Weapon Focus feat becomes an entropic weapon for you. (If you have multiple Weapon Focus feats, you extend this benefit to all of the weapons selected in this way.) Additionally, you can use a move action to make any type of weapon that you are proficient with an entropic weapon for you; you can only do this during combat against a significant opponent, and the benefit ends once that combat ends.

Entropic weapons provide many of the same benefits to you as your entropic strikes, allowing you to earn and expend EP for various effects. However, they use their own damage and weapon properties (as listed in 4 their weapon description) unless otherwise stated.

First Vanguard Aspect

Every vanguard learns to focus on one specific aspect of entropy’s role within the Multiverse. Your aspect gives you an additional understanding of the universe around you, and allows to you connect with entropy in ways that no one else can. If an aspect ability allows a target to attempt a saving throw to resist its effects (including spell-like abilities), the DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 your vanguard level + your Constitution modifier, unless stated otherwise.

You select one vanguard aspect when you take your first level of vanguard. Once made, this choice can’t be changed.

Aspect Insight: At 1st level, you gain an “Improved” combat maneuver feat, as well as a +2 insight bonus to checks with one skill determined by your aspect.
Aspect Embodiment: At 4th level, you gain an additional means of generating Entropy Points. If your aspect embodiment requires any interaction with another creature, that creature qualifies only if it is a significant enemy.
Aspect Catalyst: At 12th level, you have learned to create significant effects through your aspect. You gain an ability that you can use once per encounter either as an immediate action the first time you take a critical hit in combat, or as a standard action by expending 4 EP. You can’t use the ability again until the next time you roll initiative against a significant enemy. You also gain an improved version of the ability that you can use ? without taking an action the first time you reach 0 hit points in a combat encounter, expending all Entropy Points you have, if any. Once you use the improved version of this ability, you can’t do so again for 24 hours.
Aspect Finale: At 18th level, you gain a powerful ability unique to your aspect.
Mitigate

At 2nd level, you gain a degree of control over how damage affects you. As an immediate action when you take damage, you can spend 1 EP to reduce the damage you take by an amount equal to your vanguard level (to a minimum of 0 damage).

Additionally, as a swift action, you can remove any DR or energy resistance you have, or the AC benefit of any ability or spell that increases your AC. If the effect granting DR or energy resistance has a duration, this ends the effect entirely for you. If you end an AC benefit, that AC benefit is ended for the duration of the effect. If the ability does not normally have a duration, you suspend the listed benefits until the beginning of your next turn. In addition, whenever you first come under the effect of an ability or spell that grants you DR, energy resistance, or a bonus to AC, you can waive that benefit of the effect.

Vanguard Disciplines

Your intricate knowledge of multidisciplinary fields of study, and your mastery of the subtleties of the power of entropy—the flow of matter and energy between order and chaos—allow you to manipulate reality in complex ways known as disciplines.

You learn your first vanguard discipline at 2nd level and an additional discipline every 2 levels thereafter. Unless otherwise specified, you can’t select the same discipline more than once. If a vanguard discipline allows a saving throw to resist its effects, the DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 your vanguard level + your Constitution modifier.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 3rd level, you gain the ability to react to danger before your senses would normally allow you to do so.

You cannot be caught flat-footed, nor do you lose your Dexterity bonus to AC if your attacker is invisible. You still lose your Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. You can still lose your Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against you.

If you already have uncanny dodge from a different class, you automatically gain improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Uncanny Speed (Ex)

At 3rd level, you gain the ability to both move and attack as part of the same fluid motion. This functions as the Spring Attack feat, except that it only works when you use your entropic strikes and entropic weapons.

At 9th level, this ability works as Improved Spring Attack. At 15th level, it works as Greater Spring Attack.

Entropic Attunement (Su)

As your control over your entropic strike increases, you learn to fine-tune it with specialized effects.

The saving throw DC for any of these effects that allow a saving throw is equal to 10 + 1/2 your vanguard level + your Constitution modifier.

At 5th level, choose one of the following weapon special qualities: brace, crush, disarm, distract, shove, sunder, sweep, or trip. Once made, this choice can be changed only when you gain a new vanguard level. As long as you have at least 1 EP, your entropic strike always has the chosen special quality.

At 7th level, choose one of the following weapon special properties: anarchic, corrosive burst, or wounding. Once made, this choice can be changed only when you gain a new vanguard level. Your entropic strike gains this special weapon property as long as you have at least 1 EP.

At 10th level, your field of entropy extends far enough that you can choose to make an attack with any unarmed strike or entropic weapon as if that weapon had the reach special weapon quality. Alternatively, if an entropic weapon already has the reach special quality, you can choose to make an attack with it as if it did not have that quality. Using this ability is a free action, but you must have at least 1 EP remaining in order to use it.

At 13th level, your entropy field doubles the range increment of all ranged entropic weapons that you employ, provided you have at least 1 EP remaining.

At 16th level, you can spend 1 EP as a full-round action to make an entropic strike against every opponent within your reach. This functions as the Whirlwind Attack feat.

At 19th level, as long as you have 1 EP, your entropic strike gains a second weapon special quality, selected from those listed at 5th level. In addition, while you have at least 1 EP, your critical damage multiplier for all entropic strikes increases by 1, to a maximum of ×4.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 7th level and higher, you can no longer be flanked. This defense denies a rogue the ability to sneak attack you by flanking you, unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than you have vanguard levels.

If you already have uncanny dodge (see above) from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank you.

Second Vanguard Aspect

At 8th level, your understanding of entropy expands. Select a second vanguard aspect, which must be different from your first vanguard aspect. Once made, this choice cannot be changed.

Second Aspect Insight: At 8th level, you gain the aspect insight benefit from your second vanguard aspect. If you already have the bonus feat granted by this aspect insight, you can instead select any other feat for which you meet the prerequisites.
Second Aspect Embodiment: At 17th level, you gain the aspect embodiment benefit of the second vanguard aspect you selected at 8th level.
Flashing Strikes (Ex)

At 11th level, your mastery of melee combat allows you to make multiple attacks more accurately.

Once per round, when you miss with an unarmed strike or an attack with a melee entropic weapon, you can expend 1 EP to reroll that attack roll at the same base attack bonus. This does not stack with other abilities that allow you to reroll a missed attack roll.

Invulnerability (Su)

At 20th level, once per day as an immediate action, you become immune to the blinded, dazed, dazzled, deafened, exhausted, fatigued, paralyzed, and stunned conditions. If you are currently suffering from any of those conditions, they are suspended for the duration of this effect, but resume with their remaining duration when it ends.

You also gain immunity to critical hits (and any effects triggered by critical hits), and add your Constitution bonus to your CMD.

You can take 1 additional swift action or immediate action per round, but you can still only take 1 immediate action per triggering event.

These benefits last for 1 minute.
